baby.description: Explore 50 baby clipart designs for nursery cards, baby showers and family keepsakes. Edit online and download transparent WebP or matching CMYK PDF files.
baby.intro: Find 50 baby illustrations for personal birth announcements, nursery prints, baby-shower invitations and family scrapbooks. Explore sleeping newborns, first steps, favorite toys, playful costumes and ten black-and-white outline drawings. Choose a pose that leaves enough room for your name, date or greeting.
baby.heading: Choose a baby illustration for your keepsake
paragraphs: For a birth announcement, try a simple swaddled newborn, a baby holding a star or the sleeping crescent-moon scene. Place the name and date outside the illustration so they remain readable at small sizes. The twin-baby composition keeps both children together, while a stroller or crib makes a wider focal point for a landscape card.

For a milestone album, choose an action that matches the memory: crawling, taking first steps, trying on shoes or making handprint art. The animal costumes, astronaut, ballerina and mermaid suit imaginative birthday themes. Keep fine details such as lace, hair and basket weaving large enough to see in print.

The ten outline drawings provide a different starting point for classroom coloring and personal handmade cards. Open clothing and blanket areas leave room for color, while the stroller and crib contain finer lines. In the editor, add your own caption and shapes, arrange the image, change the background or crop the canvas; save the project to return to those changes later.
baby.print: Each design includes a transparent WebP and its matching CMYK PDF. The original canvases vary from portrait to landscape, so the gallery keeps every composition in proportion. Check the pixel dimensions and PDF page size on the individual artwork page before printing. The supplied PDF images have 600 pixels per inch at their native page size; enlarging them changes the effective print resolution.

heart.description: Browse 50 heart clipart designs: watercolor hearts, floral frames, outlines and caring gestures. Edit online or download transparent WebP and CMYK PDF files.
heart.lead: A little love for the things you make.
heart.intro: Explore 50 heart illustrations for personal Valentine's cards, wedding keepsakes, friendship notes and classroom kindness activities. Choose from glossy symbols, watercolor washes, floral wreaths, lace frames, caring hands and black-and-white designs. Every preview leads to its own matching WebP, PDF and online editor.
heart.heading: Find the right heart for your message
paragraphs: For a small label or digital greeting, start with a simple glossy heart, a solid silhouette or the clean outline. These shapes stay recognizable when reduced. Floral wreaths, lace frames and ribbon hearts leave an open center for initials or a short message; keep the lettering inside that space so it does not compete with the border.

For a personal wedding or anniversary card, try the interlocking hearts, satin ribbon, lovebirds or rose-filled envelope. The teddy bear, waving heart character and candy trio give classroom friendship notes a playful feel. Hands holding a heart, children sharing one and the puzzle-piece design suit writing prompts about care and cooperation.

Choose the mandala, geometric heart or floral outline for a coloring activity. The engraved anatomical heart and lace border have much finer detail, so allow more space when printing. Open any design in the editor to position, rotate or crop it and add separate text and shape layers. Save your project before exporting if you want to revise the layout later.
heart.print: The transparent WebP files are 1,382 × 1,382 pixels. Each matching CMYK PDF is approximately 4.61 inches square, giving 300 pixels per inch at its native size. Use the WebP for digital layouts and the PDF for printing; select actual size to keep the supplied print scale. Leave delicate watercolor and lace edges visible against a suitable background.

winter.description: Find winter clipart for classroom activities, nature journals and personal cards. Edit snowy animals, cozy characters and winter gear; download WebP or CMYK PDF.
winter.lead: Small winter stories, ready to make your own.
winter.intro: Bring a winter lesson or personal project to life with snowy wildlife, a cocoa-loving penguin, a child building a snowman and cold-weather clothing. Choose a detailed illustration for a nature journal, an expressive character for a reading prompt or a clear equipment drawing for vocabulary practice.
winter.heading: Choose a winter illustration for your activity
paragraphs: For a sequencing activity, start with the child adding a carrot nose to a snowman. Leave space beside the scene for children to write what happened before and what might happen next. The penguin holding cocoa works well beside a cozy reading prompt or a short personal greeting.

For a nature journal or wildlife vocabulary card, compare the arctic fox and the red cardinal. Give the white fox enough contrast against the page and leave room around its tail. The cardinal’s crest, beak and long tail provide clear features to describe; keep the holly branch visible when cropping.

For winter clothing and outdoor equipment lessons, use the mittens, hat, scarf, boots, skates or sled. Match the illustration to the word or action in your activity. Keep the original proportions when resizing, and use the editor to add your own captions, background and separate shapes.
winter.print: Every illustration has a matching transparent WebP, a CMYK PDF and an online editor. The newer detailed illustrations retain their native pixel dimensions and are placed at 300 pixels per inch in the original PDFs. Check each artwork page for its exact dimensions and page size. Fine fur, feathers and knitted textures need more room than simple equipment drawings; print at actual size before planning an enlargement.
